props.name: The Singleton Pattern
props.plain: A class that permits only one instance of itself and gives the whole program a single point of access to it.

props.title: The names, mapped to your code
props.plain: The class hides its constructor and exposes one static accessor that always returns the same instance.
props.gof: Ensure a class has only one instance, and provide a global point of access to it.

props.title: The pattern with the most caveats
costs: It's global state, dressed as an object
Hard to swap or reset — tests bleed state
dont: You want 'usually one' — inject it instead
You need to substitute it in tests
'One' is really a scope or lifetime concern
props.signal: a resource that is genuinely unique AND expensive AND must be shared process-wide — like a real connection pool.

props.title: Singleton, in one breath
items: Every 'new' made another copy of a resource meant to be shared — so the database's limit became a fiction.
There must be exactly one, reachable everywhere — so let the class own its instance: private constructor, one accessor.
Use the holder idiom for lazy, thread-safe creation with no locks — and reach for Singleton sparingly; it's global state.
props.challenge: An app needs one in-memory metrics registry — counters and timers every module updates, and a reporter reads once a minute.
props.question: Does Singleton truly fit — or would injecting one shared instance serve you better?
